text:
After the hospital I was referred to a community mental health team. I had a care coordinator who visited every two weeks, and a psychiatrist who prescribed an antidepressant and, for the first two months, a low-dose antipsychotic, which I think helped with the presence. After that I had a course of CBT with a psychologist. She was very good. She helped me understand that the presence was a kind of threat-detection gone into overdrive, and we did exercises like sitting with my back to the door on purpose.

Living with my parents was hard but also stabilising. My mum and I eventually talked properly, and she told me how scared she'd been. That helped us both.

I started volunteering at an animal shelter, which got me out of the house and gave me structure. Eventually I got a new job.

Unhelpful: reading forums where people described never recovering from bad trips. Also, a friend who suggested a 'healing' mushroom trip to undo the bad one.

I'm a lot better now, two years later. I still don't like mirrors in the evening.

Ich habe eine Therapie begonnen, auch um zu lernen, wie ich meine Schwester unterstützen kann, ohne mich selbst zu überfordern. Sie macht selbst eine Traumatherapie. Wir reden viel miteinander. Mit unseren Eltern haben wir inzwischen auch gesprochen. Den Onkel sehen wir nicht mehr.
Keine Horrorfilme mehr, das war die ganze Behandlung.
We talked a lot about it on the rest of the trip and after. White noise machine at night helped. It faded.

I saw a psychologist for about eight months. We worked on the claustrophobia with gradual exposure, starting with standing in a lift with the doors open, then taking one floor. That helped a lot. We also talked about my fear of death and my children, and she helped me see that the vision was about my fears, not a prophecy. I took up swimming, which helps me feel free in my body. I'm back to taking lifts, though I still don't love them.

I saw a neurologist who ran tests, which were normal, and a psychologist for the health anxiety and the fear of hospitals. We did a lot of gradual exposure, like visiting a hospital as a visitor, then having a routine blood test. My parents were very supportive. I joined a harm reduction group at university and now volunteer at their stall at festivals, handing out information about drug checking. That gives the whole thing some meaning.
Ich habe mit einer Psychologin über meine Gesundheitsangst gesprochen und gelernt, dass sie bei Medizinstudierenden gar nicht so selten ist. Das hat mir geholfen. Inzwischen ist es viel besser.
Talked to a friend, it passed.

I spoke to a chaplain at my university, which sounds odd since I'm not religious, but he was very calm and helped me separate the drug experience from questions of faith. I also saw a counsellor for a few months for the anxiety and low mood. Writing about it helped. I stopped reading about hell at night.
Gespräche mit Freundinnen haben geholfen. Ansonsten nichts Besonderes.
